7	
8	The functions in the `aws` namespace interface with various Amazon Web Services
9	APIs to make it possible for a template to render differently based on the AWS
10	environment and metadata.
11	
12	### Configuring AWS
13	
14	A number of environment variables can be used to control how gomplate communicates
15	with AWS APIs. A few are documented here for convenience. See [the `aws-sdk-go` documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-go/v1/developer-guide/configuring-sdk.html)
16	for details.
17	
18	| Environment Variable | Description |
19	| -------------------- | ----------- |
20	| `AWS_ANON` | Set to `true` when accessing services that do not need authentication, such as with public S3 buckets. Not part of the AWS SDK. |
21	| `AWS_TIMEOUT` | _(Default `500`)_ Adjusts timeout for API requests, in milliseconds. Not part of the AWS SDK. |
22	| `AWS_PROFILE` | Profile name the SDK should use when loading shared config from the configuration files. If not provided `default` will be used as the profile name. |
23	| `AWS_REGION` | Specifies where to send requests. See [this list](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html). Note that the region must be set for AWS functions to work correctly, either through this variable, through a configuration profile, or by running on an EC2 instance. |
24	| `AWS_EC2_METADATA_SERVICE_ENDPOINT` | _(Default `http://169.254.169.254`)_ Sets the base address of the instance metadata service. |
25	
26	## `aws.EC2Meta`
27	
28	**Alias:** `ec2meta`
29	
30	Queries AWS [EC2 Instance Metadata](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-metadata.html) for information. This only retrieves data in the `meta-data` path -- for data in the `dynamic` path use `aws.EC2Dynamic`.
31	
32	For times when running outside EC2, or when the metadata API can't be reached, a `default` value can be provided.
33	
34	_Added in gomplate [v1.8.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.8.0)_
35	### Usage
36	
37	```
38	aws.EC2Meta key [default]
39	```
40	
41	### Arguments
42	
43	| name | description |
44	|------|-------------|
45	| `key` | _(required)_ the metadata key to query |
46	| `default` | _(optional)_ the default value |
47	
48	### Examples
49	
50	```console
51	$ echo '{{aws.EC2Meta "instance-id"}}' | gomplate
52	i-12345678
53	```
54	
55	## `aws.EC2Dynamic`
56	
57	**Alias:** `ec2dynamic`
58	
59	Queries AWS [EC2 Instance Dynamic Metadata](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-metadata.html) for information. This only retrieves data in the `dynamic` path -- for data in the `meta-data` path use `aws.EC2Meta`.
60	
61	For times when running outside EC2, or when the metadata API can't be reached, a `default` value can be provided.
62	
63	_Added in gomplate [v1.8.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.8.0)_
64	### Usage
65	
66	```
67	aws.EC2Dynamic key [default]
68	```
69	
70	### Arguments
71	
72	| name | description |
73	|------|-------------|
74	| `key` | _(required)_ the dynamic metadata key to query |
75	| `default` | _(optional)_ the default value |
76	
77	### Examples
78	
79	```console
80	$ echo '{{ (aws.EC2Dynamic "instance-identity/document" | json).region }}' | gomplate
81	us-east-1
82	```
83	
84	## `aws.EC2Region`
85	
86	**Alias:** `ec2region`
87	
88	Queries AWS to get the region. An optional default can be provided, or returns
89	`unknown` if it can't be determined for some reason.
90	
91	_Added in gomplate [v1.8.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.8.0)_
92	### Usage
93	
94	```
95	aws.EC2Region [default]
96	```
97	
98	### Arguments
99	
100	| name | description |
101	|------|-------------|
102	| `default` | _(optional)_ the default value |
103	
104	### Examples
105	
106	_In EC2_
107	```console
108	$ echo '{{ aws.EC2Region }}' | ./gomplate
109	us-east-1
110	```
111	_Not in EC2_
112	```console
113	$ echo '{{ aws.EC2Region }}' | ./gomplate
114	unknown
115	$ echo '{{ aws.EC2Region "foo" }}' | ./gomplate
116	foo
117	```
118	
119	## `aws.EC2Tag`
120	
121	**Alias:** `ec2tag`
122	
123	Queries the AWS EC2 API to find the value of the given [user-defined tag](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Using_Tags.html). An optional default
124	can be provided.
125	
126	_Added in gomplate [v3.8.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.8.0)_
127	### Usage
128	
129	```
130	aws.EC2Tag tag [default]
131	```
132	
133	### Arguments
134	
135	| name | description |
136	|------|-------------|
137	| `tag` | _(required)_ the tag to query |
138	| `default` | _(optional)_ the default value |
139	
140	### Examples
141	
142	```console
143	$ echo 'This server is in the {{ aws.EC2Tag "Account" }} account.' | ./gomplate
144	foo
145	```
146	```console
147	$ echo 'I am a {{ aws.EC2Tag "classification" "meat popsicle" }}.' | ./gomplate
148	I am a meat popsicle.
149	```
150	
151	## `aws.EC2Tags`
152	
153	**Alias:** `ec2tags`
154	
155	Queries the AWS EC2 API to find all the tags/values [user-defined tag](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Using_Tags.html).
156	
157	_Added in gomplate [v3.8.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.8.0)_
158	### Usage
159	
160	```
161	aws.EC2Tags
162	```
163	
164	### Arguments
165	
166	| name | description |
167	|------|-------------|
168	
169	### Examples
170	
171	```console
172	echo '{{ range $key, $value := aws.EC2Tags }}{{(printf "%s=%s\n" $key $value)}}{{ end }}' | ./gomplate
173	Description=foo
174	Name=bar
175	svc:name=foobar
176	```
177	
178	## `aws.KMSEncrypt`
179	
180	Encrypt an input string with the AWS Key Management Service (KMS).
181	
182	At most 4kb (4096 bytes) of data may be encrypted.
183	
184	The resulting ciphertext will be base-64 encoded.
185	
186	The `keyID` parameter is used to reference the Customer Master Key to use,
187	and can be:
188	
189	- the key's ID (e.g. `1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab`)
190	- the key's ARN (e.g. `arn:aws:kms:us-east-2:111122223333:key/1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab`)
191	- the alias name (aliases must be prefixed with `alias/`, e.g. `alias/ExampleAlias`)
192	- the alias ARN (e.g. `arn:aws:kms:us-east-2:111122223333:alias/ExampleAlias`)
193	
194	For information on creating keys, see [_Creating Keys_](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/create-keys.html)
195	
196	See [the AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/overview.html)
197	for more details.
198	
199	See also [`aws.KMSDecrypt`](#awskmsdecrypt).
200	
201	_Added in gomplate [v4.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v4.0.0)_
202	### Usage
203	
204	```
205	aws.KMSEncrypt keyID input
206	```
207	```
208	input | aws.KMSEncrypt keyID
209	```
210	
211	### Arguments
212	
213	| name | description |
214	|------|-------------|
215	| `keyID` | _(required)_ the ID of the Customer Master Key (CMK) to use for encryption |
216	| `input` | _(required)_ the string to encrypt |
217	
218	### Examples
219	
220	```console
221	$ export CIPHER=$(gomplate -i '{{ aws.KMSEncrypt "alias/gomplate" "hello world" }}')
222	$ gomplate -i '{{ env.Getenv "CIPHER" | aws.KMSDecrypt }}'
223	```
224	
225	## `aws.KMSDecrypt`
226	
227	Decrypt ciphertext that was encrypted with the AWS Key Management Service
228	(KMS).
229	
230	The ciphertext must be base-64 encoded.
231	
232	See [the AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/overview.html)
233	for more details.
234	
235	See also [`aws.KMSEncrypt`](#awskmsencrypt).
236	
237	_Added in gomplate [v3.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.4.0)_
238	### Usage
239	
240	```
241	aws.KMSDecrypt input
242	```
243	```
244	input | aws.KMSDecrypt
245	```
246	
247	### Arguments
248	
249	| name | description |
250	|------|-------------|
251	| `input` | _(required)_ the base-64 encoded ciphertext to decrypt |
252	
253	### Examples
254	
255	```console
256	$ export CIPHER=$(gomplate -i '{{ aws.KMSEncrypt "alias/gomplate" "hello world" }}')
257	$ gomplate -i '{{ env.Getenv "CIPHER" | aws.KMSDecrypt }}'
258	```
259	
260	## `aws.Account`
261	
262	Returns the currently-authenticated AWS account ID number.
263	
264	Wraps the [STS GetCallerIdentity API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_GetCallerIdentity.html)
265	
266	See also [`aws.UserID`](#awsuserid) and [`aws.ARN`](#awsarn).
267	
268	_Added in gomplate [v3.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.4.0)_
269	### Usage
270	
271	```
272	aws.Account
273	```
274	
275	
276	### Examples
277	
278	```console
279	$ gomplate -i 'My account is {{ aws.Account }}'
280	My account is 123456789012
281	```
282	
283	## `aws.ARN`
284	
285	Returns the AWS ARN (Amazon Resource Name) associated with the current authentication credentials.
286	
287	Wraps the [STS GetCallerIdentity API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_GetCallerIdentity.html)
288	
289	See also [`aws.UserID`](#awsuserid) and [`aws.Account`](#awsaccount).
290	
291	_Added in gomplate [v3.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.4.0)_
292	### Usage
293	
294	```
295	aws.ARN
296	```
297	
298	
299	### Examples
300	
301	```console
302	$ gomplate -i 'Calling from {{ aws.ARN }}'
303	Calling from arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/Alice
304	```
305	
306	## `aws.UserID`
307	
308	Returns the unique identifier of the calling entity. The exact value
309	depends on the type of entity making the call. The values returned are those
310	listed in the `aws:userid` column in the [Principal table](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_variables.html#principaltable)
311	found on the Policy Variables reference page in the IAM User Guide.
312	
313	Wraps the [STS GetCallerIdentity API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_GetCallerIdentity.html)
314	
315	See also [`aws.ARN`](#awsarn) and [`aws.Account`](#awsaccount).
316	
317	_Added in gomplate [v3.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.4.0)_
318	### Usage
319	
320	```
321	aws.UserID
322	```
323	
324	
325	### Examples
326	
327	```console
328	$ gomplate -i 'I am {{ aws.UserID }}'
329	I am AIDACKCEVSQ6C2EXAMPLE
330	```

7	
8	The functions in the `gcp` namespace interface with various Google Cloud Platform
9	APIs to make it possible for a template to render differently based on the GCP
10	environment and metadata.
11	
12	### Configuring GCP
13	
14	A number of environment variables can be used to control how gomplate communicates
15	with GCP APIs.
16	
17	| Environment Variable | Description |

args.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/probe && cat > /tmp/probe/srv.py <<'EOF'
import http.server, sys, json
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def _h(self):
        sys.stderr.write(f"REQ {self.command} {self.path} headers={dict(self.headers)}\n")
        p = self.path
        if 'instance-identity' in p:
            body = json.dumps({"region":"us-west-2","instanceId":"i-0abcdef"}).encode()
        elif p.endswith('/instance-id'):
            body = b'i-0abcdef'
        else:
            body = b'VALUE:' + p.encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header('Content-Type','text/plain')
        self.send_header('Content-Length',str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)
    do_GET = _h
    do_PUT = _h
http.server.HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', int(sys.argv[1])), H).serve_forever()
EOF
(python3 /tmp/probe/srv.py 18080 2>/tmp/probe/log_aws.txt &) ; (python3 /tmp/probe/srv.py 18081 2>/tmp/probe/log_gcp.txt &) ; sleep 0.5; echo started

$X -i '{{ base64.DecodeBytes "AAAA" | crypto.DecryptAES "swordfish" }}' 2>&1 | grep -o 'error calling.*'
# 16-byte all-zero input (bad padding likely)
$X -i '{{ base64.DecodeBytes "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA==" | crypto.DecryptAES "swordfish" }}' 2>&1 | grep -o 'error calling.*'
# 32-byte input, wrong padding
$X -i '{{ base64.DecodeBytes "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=" | crypto.DecryptAES "swordfish" }}' 2>&1 | grep -o 'error calling.*'
# 3-byte string input
$X -i '{{ "abc" | crypto.DecryptAES "swordfish" }}' 2>&1 | grep -o 'error calling.*'
# EncryptAES with bad keyBits type
$X -i '{{ crypto.EncryptAES "k" "abc" "in" }}' 2>&1 | grep -o 'error calling.*'
# EncryptAES 192 roundtrip
$X -i '{{ "data" | crypto.EncryptAES "pw" 192 | crypto.DecryptAES "pw" 192 }}'
# default 256 roundtrip
$X -i '{{ "data" | crypto.EncryptAES "pw" | crypto.DecryptAES "pw" }}'
# keyBits given as 3rd? pipeline: input | EncryptAES key keyBits
$X -i '{{ "data" | crypto.EncryptAES "pw" | crypto.DecryptAES "pw" 256 }}'

payload.resultSummary:
Only mismatch is the `dict` global, which belongs to another agent and isn't implemented yet — my conversion of maps is already verified via unit test (`%v` formatting). Everything else matches byte-for-byte.

## Final report

**Files created (all mine, package `funcs`):**
- `/workspace/src/internal/funcs/filepath.go` — `filepath` namespace + shared `pathArgToString` helper
- `/workspace/src/internal/funcs/path.go` — `path` namespace
- `/workspace/src/internal/funcs/path_test.go` — unit tests for both

**`filepath.*` implemented (12):** `Base`, `Clean`, `Dir`, `Ext`, `FromSlash`, `IsAbs`, `Join`, `Match`, `Rel`, `Split`, `ToSlash`, `VolumeName` — thin wrappers over stdlib `path/filepath`.

**`path.*` implemented (8):** `Base`, `Clean`, `Dir`, `Ext`, `IsAbs`, `Join`, `Match`, `Split` — wrappers over stdlib `path`.

**Skipped (binary lacks them — verified via `can't evaluate field ... in type interface {}`):** `filepath.Abs`, `filepath.Glob`, `filepath.EvalSymlinks`, `filepath.Localize`, `path.Rel`, `path.FromSlash`, `path.ToSlash`, `path.VolumeName`, `path.Abs`, `path.Glob`.

**Global aliases:** none for either namespace (verified `pathBase`, `filepathClean` etc. are `not defined`; `join` belongs to coll).

**Behavior notes (probed from the binary, matched exactly):**
- Args are converted with nil → `"nil"` (special case), everything else via `fmt.Sprintf("%v", in)`: `4.0`→`"4"`, `1e21`→`"1e+21"`, `0.00001`→`"1e-05"`, `true`→`"true"`, `map[string]int{a:1}`→`"map[a:1]"`.
- `Join` is variadic over `interface{}` and stringifies each element: `{{ path.Join "a" 1 true }}` → `a/1/true`; zero args → `""`; `nil` element → `"nil"`.
- Wrong arg counts produce text/template's stock `wrong number of args for Base: want 1 got 2` (fixed-arity methods reproduce this automatically).
- `Match(pattern, name)` returns `(bool, error)`; bad pattern surfaces as `error calling Match: syntax error in pattern`; empty pattern with non-empty name returns `false` with no error.
- `Rel` passes stdlib errors through: `error calling Rel: Rel: can't make /b relative to a`; `Rel "" ""` → `.`.
- `Split` returns `[]string{dir, file}` (prints as `[/tmp/ foo]`, empty input → `[ ]`).

**Verification:** `go test -buildvcs=false ./internal/funcs/ -run 'TestFilePath|TestPath'` — 10/10 pass. Differential script of 49 templates (values, edge inputs, pipelines, error cases) against `/workspace/executable` — all match except one template using the not-yet-implemented `dict` global (another agent's function; my map formatting is unit-tested instead).

**Known remaining mismatches:** none in my scope.

payload.resultSummary:
Env namespace is complete. Summary:

## Files owned/modified
- `/workspace/src/internal/funcs/env.go` — fully rewritten (package `funcs`, namespace object `Env` self-registers in `init()`)
- `/workspace/src/internal/funcs/env_test.go` — new unit tests (5 tests, all pass)

## Functions implemented (all verified byte-for-byte against the binary)

- **`env.Getenv(key interface{}, def ...string) string`** — variadic so the binary's exact template errors reproduce: 0 args → `wrong number of args for Getenv: want at least 1 got 0`; non-string default → `expected string; found 42`. Behavior: `os.Getenv(key)`; if the value is **empty string** (not just unset), falls back to the `key_FILE` variant (file contents, trailing `\r\n` trimmed via `strings.TrimRight(s, "\r\n")`, interior newlines/CRs preserved; unreadable/missing file → `""` silently); if still empty, first default arg wins (extra defaults ignored). Non-string keys (`42`, `true`) are stringified via `fmt.Sprintf("%v")` and looked up (→ `""` when unset).
- **`env.Env() map[string]string`** — built from `os.Environ()`, splits on first `=`, skips malformed entries. `{{ env.Env }}` prints sorted `map[...]`; `{{ env.Env.MISSING }}` errors with `map has no entry for key ...`; `{{ index env.Env "PATH" }}` works. No `_FILE` fallback (matches docs + binary).
- **`env.HasEnv(key interface{}) bool`** — exactly 1 arg (2 args → `wrong number of args for HasEnv: want 1 got 2`); wraps `os.LookupEnv`, so a var set to empty string returns `true`. Non-string keys stringified (`env.HasEnv 42` → `false`).
- **`env.ExpandEnv(input interface{}) string`** — exactly 1 arg; `os.Expand` with the Getenv mapping, so `$VAR`/`${VAR}` expand with the same `_FILE` fallback and trim rules; undefined vars → empty string; `$$` and lone `$` pass through per stdlib rules. `env.ExpandEnv 42` → `"42"`.

## Global aliases registered
- **`getenv`** → same `Env.Getenv` function (verified: value/default/_FILE/0-arg error `wrong number of args for getenv: want at least 1 got 0` all match).

## Functions probed but skipped (binary lacks them)
- No `hasenv`/`expandenv`/`env` global aliases other than `getenv` (`hasenv` → `function "hasenv" not defined`).
- No `env.GetenvBool`, `GetenvInt`, `Expand`, `LookupEnv`, `Environ`, `GetEnv`, `ParseEnv`, `Bool`, `Int`, `List`, `Keys` — all return `can't evaluate field ...` in the binary.

## Verification
- `go test ./internal/funcs/ -run TestEnv` — 5/5 pass (set/unset/empty vars, defaults, `_FILE` incl. CRLF trim and precedence, HasEnv, ExpandEnv, Env map).
- A 40-case differential script (`/tmp/envdiff.sh`) comparing `/workspace/executable` vs my build on identical environments, covering normal use, pipelines, `_FILE` precedence (direct > file > default), empty-var fallthrough, CRLF/multi-newline trimming, missing files, all arg-count/type error messages (timestamps normalized in JSON error logs) — **all match**.
- `go build` and `go vet` clean. No shared files touched; the only registration additions are the `env` namespace (already existed) and the `getenv` global.

Known remaining mismatches: none observed.
